text:
Recent evaluation research cautions against treating diagnostic improvements as evidence of recommendation gains. [RecSys 2025’s sampling-reliability study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines whether sampled evaluations recover full-preference model rankings; earlier [sequential-recommendation experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045) found that both uniform and popularity-based negatives can reverse model ordering. Thus, HR@10 against 99 negatives and full-catalog HR@10 measure different ranking challenges. No located evidence establishes diagnostic probes as reliable predictors of gains across these exact four Amazon datasets.

Practical implication: use scale-invariant probes—positive-item rank percentile, pairwise win rate, and Kendall/Spearman agreement across identical candidate sets—rather than raw score margins. Quantify sampled/full-catalog disagreement using validation-target hit-status disagreement, target-rank percentiles, and model-order reversals across trials. Comparing top-10 lists drawn from different candidate universes directly confounds candidate availability with ranking quality. Keep full-catalog diagnostics supplementary; retain the pinned sampled macro HR@10 for selection. These are proposed diagnostic choices, not experimentally established gains.

For uncertainty, bootstrap paired per-user hit differences within each category, then average the four category means equally; report 95% intervals for category and macro improvements. [Ranking-metric research](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-020-09377-x) supports paired user-level comparisons. Such intervals condition on the trained models and fixed candidates; they do not measure training-seed or negative-sampling variability. Test probe-guided changes through one-factor ablations against SASRec, preserving seeds, splits, candidates and training budget. Record both probe changes and validation HR@10 changes; require consistent evidence across categories before claiming diagnostic usefulness. Repeated adaptive validation search also makes nominal confidence intervals optimistic.
